page.layout: One page of text in a single column; running head at top; a large initial "D" hanging in the left margin beside the paragraph beginning "Hæc de nomine"; no other marginal notes.

main_text.p: Si hoc dicit Epiphanius, fruftra eft, sed meo animo non videtur hoc dicere. Ponam ipsius verba:

p.i: ἦν δὲ καὶ Σαδοὺκ τὶς ᾿Ιουδαῖος τὴν νόμον κατὰ τὸ παλαιὸν τῶν ἱερέων · ἀλλ᾽ οὐκ ἐνέμειναν οὗτοι ἐν τῇ ᾿Ιουδαίων διδασκαλία·

main_text.p: id est, Fuit priscis temporibus sacerdos quidam nomine Sadoc, sed non manserunt isti in præsulis sui doctrina.

Quod Epiphanius hic ait, verissimum est: Sadoc autem à quo Saducæi, discipulus fuit Antigoni Sochæi. R. Nathan in vitis patrum. Iehielides in Lexico iuris. Elias Germanus Tisbite. Amplius reperio citatum ex libro Alcosder Iudæ Leuitæ.
„ Ezdras Cabalam tradidit Simeoni Iusto: is Antigono, & socijs „ ipsius, è quibus Sadoc & Baithos hæresiarchæ, unde Saducæi & „ Baithusæi.

Hæc de nomine: in quo falluntur qui à iustitia appellatos censent Saducæos. De doctrina res clarior. Negabant resurrectionem argumentis ab absurdo Matth. 22, 23. à non scripto, ut quod refutat ibidem ὀ σωτὴρ.

Item dicebant, Si patres nostri sciuissent mortuos resurrecturos, & præmia manere iustos post hanc vitam, non tam sæpe rebellassent. Iehielides in loco memorato: Reijciebant traditiones patrum, adeoq. omnem omnino Legis expositionem. Ioseph Ben Gorion Histor. suæ lib. 4 cap. 29.
הנרי התרוקים אומרים לא נאמין ולא נשמע לפל מסורת ולכל פירוש כי אם לתורת משה לכר:
id est, Ecce Saducæi dicebant, Ne credamus neque auscultemus vlli traditioni, aut vlli expositioni, sed tantum legi Mosis. Elias Leuita Germanus in Tisbite:
כפרי בתורה שבעל פה ולא האמינו רק מה שכתוב בתורה שבכתב עלכן קורין להם קראים לשון מקרא:
id est, Negabant legem oretenus traditam, & non credebant, nisi quod extat in lege scripta: Ideo vocati sunt Caraim. nam μικεῖ scriptura.

De Pharisæis asseuerabant quòd se miserè affligerent in hac vita propter traditiones, neque tamen in altera vita, quod esse credebant, mercedem inde vllam reportarent. Nathan Iustus Iehielides, Nata hæc hæresis ex dicto quodam Antigoni fortasse sequius accepto quàm ipse

page.notes: Hebrew and Greek lines transcribed as best read; the Greek lines near "ἦν δὲ" and the Hebrew lines are partly uncertain and may contain errors. The word "μικεῖ" after "nam" is doubtful (probably μικρα or similar Greek). The large initial D is marked as a hanging initial.
